customManagers.description: Released harmon-devkit tag pinned by root and template skills-sync manifests
Devcontainer Dockerfile ARG pins — suffix-matched so the template's Dockerfile.jinja (inside a jinja-named directory) is managed too

Workflow and composite-action tool pins (both layers), `version:`/`<tool>_version:` style. Composite actions are included because template/.github/actions/setup/action.yml.jinja pins setup-task and setup-tflint this way, and a `workflows/`-only pattern leaves them invisible here — the same silent rot the SHA manager below was added for.

Workflow/composite-action and script tool pins, `FOO_VERSION=x.y.z` shell-variable style. Template scripts carry jinja in the FILENAME (`…foo.sh[% endif %]`), so the .sh alternative tolerates that suffix — without it every pin under template/scripts/ is invisible here.

GitHub Action SHA pins (`uses: owner/repo@sha # vX.Y.Z`) in the template's .jinja workflows AND composite actions — the native github-actions manager can't parse the .jinja extension, so these pins rotted silently until the omator retro caught them. `actions/` is covered too: template/.github/actions/setup/action.yml.jinja pins setup-node, setup-python, setup-uv, setup-terraform and setup-tflint by SHA. Conditional workflow filenames (`…yml[% endif %].jinja`) must stay matched or their pins rot the same way.

Taskfile tool pins (root Taskfile + included taskfiles/, both layers), `FOO_VERSION: x.y.z` var style — used by foreman:lint's uvx-pinned ruff/black. The taskfiles pattern tolerates a trailing jinja conditional in the directory name (template/[% if use_foreman %]taskfiles[% endif %]/) — without it the template twin's pins are invisible to Renovate and only the root copy gets bumped, which fails test:dogfood-parity

packageRules.description: Wait 3 days before proposing any update
Batch all GitHub Actions updates into one PR
Batch regex-managed workflow and composite-action updates into one PR — the composite action provisions the same CI toolchain the workflows do, so its pins belong in the same batch
Batch all Docker image updates into one PR

Batch all devcontainer updates (base image + annotated tools) into one PR — must come after the Docker images rule so the base image lands here instead. Root scripts/** and taskfiles/** are included because every regex-managed pin under them (@devcontainers/cli, semgrep, markdownlint-cli2, ruff, black) is a dogfood-parity twin of a template/** copy this rule already claims — a dep whose root and template copies resolve to different groups gets split across two PRs, and each fails test:dogfood-parity. In this repo the group is effectively 'devcontainer + template-shipped tool pins'

Template workflow AND composite-action pins belong with the GitHub Actions batch, not the Devcontainer batch — must come after the Devcontainer rule (which claims all of template/**) so this override wins. Composite actions are listed explicitly: template/.github/actions/setup/action.yml.jinja pins setup-node/-python/-uv/-terraform/-task/-tflint, and without this line they would all be filed as Devcontainer updates
Surface harmon-devkit releases for deliberate pin-and-sync updates
prBodyNotes: Normally unnecessary: `.github/workflows/sync-harmon-devkit.yml` already opens a complete pin-and-sync PR on every stable harmon-devkit release. This rule stays as a passive stale-pin signal and manual fallback: dashboard-gating means it never opens a pin PR unattended, but approving it while the automation is healthy produces a SECOND PR for the same bump. Leave it unapproved unless the workflow is broken and you are deliberately falling back to the manual route.

If you do approve this update, run `task sync:skills` and push the refreshed `.claude/skills/` as a separate commit; do not amend Renovate's commit. A ref-only bump fails the skills drift check by design.

packageRules.description: Batch the web-astro test-fixture dependency bumps into one PR (the fixture validates the shipped ESLint config; its deps move together)
Batch the web-app test-fixture dependency bumps into one PR

Eject anthropics/claude-code-action from the batched GitHub Actions group and skip the 3-day release-age wait. It ships near-daily first-party releases, so grouping + minimumReleaseAge kept the whole Actions batch perpetually pending on the renovate/stability-days gate — each rebase pulled in a fresh release and reset the 3-day clock. It's a trusted first-party action and all updates are reviewed manually (automerge is off globally). Must come LAST so this override wins over every grouping rule (GitHub Actions, Devcontainer, template workflow pins).
